paragraphs: Chigwell is not a place people leave in a hurry. The houses are large, the plots are generous, and the setting, wrapped around a historic village and backed by Epping Forest, is hard to better. So the work here is rarely about needing more space to cope. It is about making an already good house even better: a bigger kitchen, a proper entertaining space, an annexe, a home that finally does everything the family wants.

We design and build those extensions across Chigwell, and we run the job as one team, from the first visit through the design, the planning and the building regulations to the finished room. On a recent project nearby in Woodford we built a full-width extension and turned a cut-up ground floor into a single open-plan space, which is the kind of work Chigwell's homes lend themselves to.

planning.title: Planning permission in Chigwell
paragraphs: Here is a useful quirk of Chigwell worth knowing before you sketch anything. So many homes here are detached, and detached houses get the more generous permitted development allowances, a deeper rear extension than a semi or terrace is allowed, for instance. That means a lot can be done here without a full application.

Two things rein that in. The first is the Green Belt. Epping Forest District is around 92 per cent Green Belt, and much of the land around Chigwell falls within it, which caps how much you can add before the work becomes a disproportionate addition to the original house. It bites hardest on large outbuildings and annexes. The second is the Chigwell Village conservation area, the historic core around the 12th-century church of St Mary the Virgin and the old Kings Head, the inn Dickens turned into the Maypole. In a conservation area some permitted development rights fall away, and design and materials are judged properly.

Being close to Epping Forest brings the usual question too. The forest is a protected area with a zone of influence around it, but that mainly affects proposals that create a new, separate home, not a normal extension to the house you live in. Your planning authority is Epping Forest District Council, and we check exactly where your property stands, then prepare and manage any application for you.

ground.title: The ground around Chigwell
paragraphs: Chigwell sits on London Clay, with the Roding valley running along its western edge. London Clay swells in the wet and shrinks in dry spells, and it moves most near large trees, of which the leafy plots here have plenty. Closer to the Roding the ground can be softer and wetter.

On a big plot with mature trees, foundations often need to go deeper than people expect, and that is worth designing for from the start rather than discovering halfway down a trench. On trickier ground we will get it checked before we price the groundworks.

cost.title: What an extension costs in Chigwell
paragraphs: Cost comes down to size, specification, the amount of structural work and the finish. Chigwell briefs tend to be larger and higher spec than average, which is reflected in the figure.

As a general guide, single-storey extensions commonly run at a few thousand pounds per square metre of finished space, with double storey often better value per square metre. Those are ballpark numbers, not a quote. Use our cost calculator for an early estimate, and book a free site visit for a real, itemised figure on your project.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for an extension in Chigwell?
faqs.a: Often not. Chigwell's many detached homes get the more generous permitted development allowances, so a good deal can be done without a full application. But the Chigwell Village conservation area reduces those rights in the old village, and the Green Belt caps overall scale. We check your exact address with Epping Forest District Council and handle any application.

faqs.q: Can I extend my house if it is in the Green Belt?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. The Green Belt does not ban extensions, it limits how much you can add before the work becomes a disproportionate addition to the original house. Well-judged schemes are approved regularly. We design to what the rules allow from the start.

faqs.q: Why does the local ground matter for my foundations?
faqs.a: Chigwell sits on London Clay, which moves with the seasons and near large trees, and the ground softens towards the Roding valley. That often means deeper or specially designed foundations, so we check the ground before starting.

faqs.q: Which areas around Chigwell do you cover?
faqs.a: Chigwell itself, including the old village, Chigwell Row and Grange Hill, along with Buckhurst Hill, Loughton, Woodford and the wider area. Call us to confirm your postcode.
